newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM'S SPITAELS SAYS WILL COOPERATE IN PS PROBE.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM'S SPITAELS SAYS WILL COOPERATE IN PS PROBE.

text.p: The Walloon Parliament received on Thursday a request for its president Guy Spitaels to be questioned by police investigating corruption in the socialist party (PS) in the late 1980s, the Belga news agency said.
RTBF radio said the request to lift Spitaels' parliamentary immunity had come from the Liege court charged with overseeing the bribes probe, but a court spokesman declined to comment.
Spitaels, who was chairman of the French-speaking socialist party at the time the bribes are alleged to have been paid, said in a statement he would cooperate fully with investigators.

He reiterated he was totally "oblivious to the allegations made in the so-called Dassault affair" and to statements said to have been made by Merry Hermanus, one of the PS party officials arrested in connection with the probe, who implicated him.
"I will make myself willingly available and give my full agreement to help establish, as soon as possible, the whole truth in the dossier that motivates this demand," he said.
Spitaels' statement followed the arrest this week of two senior PS members on charges of corruption connected to an army contract concluded with French defence firm Dassault in 1989.
A third man, a former Belgian army colonel, was charged, but not arrested, in connection with the affair on Wednesday.
No one was available at Spitaels office to comment.
The corruption allegations have shaken Belgium's four-party, centre-left coalition government, of which the French-speaking socialist party is the second largest member.
